overall_reason: A Webflow build with colour tokens (--white, --black, --fossil) that rules bypass half the time: the article page shows four near-black inks, three near-identical light greys, body text at 18, 19 and 20px and five radii across its cards and images.

score.reason: T-DRIFT-PAIRS and T-VALUE-INVENTORY fail on inks, greys, body sizes and radii; T-HARDCODE fails on retyped colour literals (TOK-010, TOK-001, TOK-004, TOK-006).

findings.evidence: Dark text runs in four near-black values: the article h2 is #131314, the nav links #000000, the story header link #020202, another heading #0f0f0f (near_duplicates #131314/#0f0f0f), and body copy is #020202 at 0.72 alpha. Secondary text pairs #727272 (story card category) with #6c6e74 (near_duplicates, 0.017 OKLab).
findings.after: One ink token and one muted-text token, referenced by every heading, link and category label
findings.why: The inks differ by less than the eye can see, so they only add values to keep in step.
findings.root: no ink or muted-text role token

findings.where: article body, CTA and story cards, 1440
findings.evidence: Body-sized text uses three sizes a step apart: the rich-text article and the timestamp are 19px (61 elements), the CTA paragraph 'text-size-medium' 20px (14) and the story-card link 18px (3) (values.1440.font_size, near_duplicates 18/19 and 19/20).
findings.after: One body size for running text and one for card links, from a declared type scale
findings.why: Readers meet three body sizes on one page, and the CTA paragraph looks slightly off against the article.

findings.evidence: The page's containers use five radii: the post container 8px, the story cards 12px, the hero image 16px, the CTA image 20px and the nav button 4px (values.1440.radius examples). All 676 radius declarations are literals.
findings.before: 4, 8, 12, 16 and 20px radii on containers and images
findings.after: Two radii: one for controls (4px) and one for cards and images (16px)
findings.why: The cards and the images beside them do the same framing job with different corners.

findings.evidence: Light fills pair #efefef (story cards), #f5f5f5 (story header button) and #ebebeb (near_duplicates, 0.018 OKLab).
findings.why: Three greys a hair apart make the surfaces look unevenly lit.

findings.evidence: Colour declarations are 52% literal (1254 literal against 1062 var), 218 colour literals equal a declared token's value, and the dark section variants (.section.dark, .footer-statement.dark-mode) set 36 literal colours such as rgb(22, 22, 22) and rgb(179, 179, 179) (theme.dark_rules_colour_declarations).
findings.after: Rules and the dark section variants reference the colour tokens
findings.why: A brand colour change then misses half the rules, including the dark sections.

findings.evidence: z-index values jump from 0, 1 and 5 to 900, 1000 and 5000 (values.1440.ladder.over_1000) with no layer token.
findings.after: A short named layer ladder (base, sticky, overlay, modal)
findings.why: Escalating layers invite the next overlay to add another zero.

strengths: Spacing sits mostly on an 8px scale (share 0.773 against chance 0.175), with 24, 16, 32 and 64px reused for section rhythm.
One family (Suisse Intl) sets every text element.
not_investigated: inline style attributes: the DOM records computed styles only
token source files behind the shipped CSS (Sass, JSON tokens, Figma variables): only the shipped CSS was read
states the capture did not open (hover, focus, open menus): their values are not in the table
the client showcase colours declared as root tokens (--attentia-dark-blue and others) belong to case-study exhibits and were not judged as the page's palette
